key_insight: ClinVerse moves medical-agent training and evaluation beyond static questions to interactive diagnostic encounters grounded in real-world health records.
clinical_relevance: The environment tests how agents gather patient information, request examinations, and reach diagnoses, without establishing readiness for clinical use.
method: Builds on ClinPatient, a dataset of 150,000 diagnostic cases derived from electronic health records.
Coordinates six specialized clinical roles as a doctor agent interviews patients and requests examinations.
Uses rule-based trajectory scores for information acquisition, examination ordering, and diagnostic accuracy as training rewards and evaluation metrics.
evidence_signal: Across general-purpose and medical-domain models, the abstract reports that nine self-evolution methods in three categories consistently improved diagnostic capabilities within ClinVerse.
watch_item: Improvements within this simulated environment do not establish patient safety or effectiveness in real clinical workflows.
paper_title: ClinVerse: A Realistic Multi-Agent Diagnostic Environment for Training and Evaluating Medical Agents
